record.paper_title: Twenty Open Problems in Enumeration of Matchings: Progress Report
record.context_brief: Hexagon with three missing border triangles
record.original_question: Determine the number of rhombus tilings of a hexagon with side lengths a, b+3, c, a+3, b, c+3 when one arbitrary triangular region is removed from each of the three longer sides.

evidence.quote: Problem 3: Theresia Eisenkölbl solved this problem. What she does in fact is to compute the number of all rhombus tilings of a hexagon with sides a, b+3, c, a+3, b, c+3 where an arbitrary triangle is removed from each of the "long" sides of the hexagon

artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider a hexagon drawn on the triangular lattice in the plane with consecutive side lengths $a,\ b+3,\ c,\ a+3,\ b,\ c+3$ (where $a,b,c$ are nonnegative integers), so that the hexagon is partitioned into unit equilateral triangles pointing alternately up and down. A rhombus tiling is a tiling of the hexagon by unit rhombi, each formed by gluing one up-triangle and one down-triangle that share an edge. On each of the three "long" sides (of lengths $b+3$, $a+3$, $c+3$), fix an arbitrarily chosen unit triangle lying along that side and remove it from the region. Determine a closed-form expression (as a function of $a,b,c$ and of the three positions of the removed triangles along the long sides) for the number of rhombus tilings of the resulting region.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was solved by Theresia Eisenkölbl, who derived an explicit product/determinant formula for the number of rhombus tilings of such a hexagon with one arbitrary unit triangle removed from each of the three long sides.

status_evidence.title: Rhombus Tilings of a Hexagon with Three Fixed Border Tiles
